newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips in busy trade, depos edge down.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips in busy trade, depos edge down.

text.p: The Polish zloty slipped slightly in active trade on an early bout of dollar buying on the back of the U.S. unit's bouyancy on world markets only to return to the three percent from parity level later on Thursday.

Dealers said the market found balance at three percent from the trading band centre as the recent pro-zloty sentiment, which pushed the local unit above 3.2 percent earlier this week, may have started to fade.
"The zloty seems comfortable at three percent and it may stay around there until the market gets another strong impulse," said Piotr Czyzewski, dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 3.03/2.98 percent from the parity rate, softer than Wednedsay's close 3.09/3.04 percent.
It closed at 2.8960/70 to the dollar, down from 2.8885/00 on Wednesday and at 1.8371/81 to the mark, flat from 1.8373/83.

Dealers also said the zloty may have lost ground against the basket on Thursday because banks extended currency exposure for next Monday, which is today's value date, after keeping long higher yielding zloty positions for the weekend.
One-day deposit rates dipped slightly in late trade, most likely after slighly larger than expected cash inflows from the clearing house, but trade remained balanced, dealers said.
"Rates fell slightly in the afternoon, probably because of inflows from the electronic clearing house, which may have created a little surplus," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.

Wieczorkiewicz said today's central bank drainage operations, which cleared some 160 million zlotys in NBP-bills and 25 million in a reverse repo, were large enough to soak up excess cash from the market but still keep it balanced.
Overnight rates closed at 21.70/21.88 percent, down a touch from 21.80/21.95 at opening and tomorrow/next at 21.70/21.90, down from 21.80/22.00. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
